verdicts.note: The cited facts hold: Google calls Play Integrity the recommended way to get platform key attestation (blog, 19 Nov 2025); since May 2025 MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY on Android 13+ needs a hardware-backed verified boot verdict; Google steers custom verifiers to its Kotlin library; the roots JSON now returns 2 certificates and a new EC root signs from 1 Feb 2026; RKP expiry must be checked; @peculiar/asn1-android only parses.
verdicts.correction: The premise that both checks rest on the same hardware signal holds only on Android 13 and higher. On Android 7 to 12, MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY carries no hardware-backed proof, while key attestation's RootOfTrust (deviceLocked, verifiedBootState) is hardware-backed wherever attestation runs in the TEE or StrongBox, which Google's note says became required from Android 8.0. Key attestation also proves the app identity through attestationApplicationId (SHA-256 digests of the signing certificates), so on its own it covers both claims of line 78 with no Google quota, no service account and no call to Google. Dropping the own verifier therefore weakens Android 7 to 12 phones and puts every Android registration under the 10,000 per day cap that cannot be raised while the app is GitHub-only (S08-02). Which single check stays is an owner decision tied to Play distribution, not a pure simplification.

verdicts.correction: The iPhone half does not hold. An App Attest key is usable only after attestKey succeeds: Apple's flow is generate, attest, then assert, and the server learns the public key only from credCert inside the attestation. So on iPhone there is no 'hardware key now, attestation later': registration needs a successful Apple call, and a phone whose attestKey keeps failing has no signing key at all. Apple says throttling and some network failures surface as errors here, and a 2026 developer report shows persistent invalidKey on iPhone 8, X and XR with iOS 16.7 to 18.7 (about 0.01 percent of users). Dropping the software key is still right, but the plan must name the fallback for an iPhone with no attested key: the existing 'hoca elle ekler' path, or a labelled keychain key kept only for that case.

recommendation_issues.problem: The text leads with Play Integrity as the single Android check. For the plan's main channel (GitHub APK) that runs into the research's own S08-02: 10,000 warm-ups and 10,000 decodes per day with no raise path off Play, so a registration wave above that labels phones 'Cihaz doğrulanmadı' through no fault of the student. It is also weaker on Android 7 to 12, where MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY has no hardware-backed proof, and it needs a server-side Google API client and a service account secret the plan does not list (see the miss on line 589). Key attestation alone has none of these limits and also proves the app's signing certificate. The research already lists the choice as an open question; that is where it belongs, and the recommendation text should not pre-decide it.

'doğrulama sonraki açılışta kendiliğinden yeniden denenir': every retry is a token preparation that counts toward the same 10,000 daily cap. On a day the cap is hit, every unverified phone retrying on every launch keeps it exhausted. Retries need a ceiling, for example at most once a day per phone and only when the server says quota is left.

'Sunucu her iPhone için iki sayaç tutar' splits one App Attest key's single counter into two server-side sequences. That departs from Apple's step 5 (greater than the previous assertion) and from WWDC26's warning that a steady or decreasing counter may mean a compromised copy, and it is only safe if record bytes and request bytes are domain-separated so one cannot be replayed as the other, which the text does not say. A simpler design keeps Apple's rule as written: App Attest assertions sign only records and device operations; the time certificate needs no student identity, and downloads use a session token issued at registration. Then counter order equals queue order, and the research's other rules (in-order queue, 'zaten var' before the counter check, the rest of a batch gets 'tekrar dene') are enough.

It carries the two-counter design from S08-04 ('son kayıt sayacı, son istek sayacı'); with the simpler design one counter per key is enough. node-app-attest returns the receipt but does not verify it, so Apple's 'verify and store' would be custom code; since the research itself advises against using the risk metric, storing the receipt as received is enough.

Reading apple_validation_category_01 and apple_bundle_version_01 must treat their absence as normal: they exist only on iOS 27 and later while the plan supports iOS 16.4 and up. As written ('başka bir değer ... kaydı işaretler') a careless implementation would label every iPhone below iOS 27. 'Kendi koduma alırım' is less cheap than stated because the package depends on cbor, asn1js and pkijs.

It removes the software key on both platforms, but the 'no attestation yet, just label it' fallback exists only on Android. On iPhone a key cannot sign anything the server can check until attestKey succeeds, so a phone whose attestation keeps failing has no key at all. The recommendation must name the fallback for that phone: the plan's 'hoca elle ekler' path, or a labelled keychain key kept only for this case.

'@peculiar/asn1-android ve @noble/curves çıkar, yeni araç eklenmez (eksi 2)' ignores that Play Integrity standard tokens can be decoded only by Google's decodeIntegrityToken endpoint with a service account access token, which needs google-auth-library or hand-written OAuth code on the server. If Play Integrity stays as the Android check, the net change is at most minus 1.

misses.finding: App Attest keys can become invalid without the student deleting the app. Apple's docs say keys do not survive reinstallation, device migration or backup restore, and Apple DTS (Feb 2025) confirmed that apps offloaded and later reloaded hit the same invalidKey error; the only remedy is a new key plus a new attestation, which needs Apple's server. In this offline-first design the phone finds out only when generateAssertion fails, possibly in class without internet, so that check-in cannot be signed. The plan covers only deliberate deletion and does not detect the loss early.

Uygulama her açılışta, internet varken anahtarla telefonda küçük bir deneme onayı üretir (sunucuya gitmez); 'geçersiz anahtar' gelirse yeni anahtarı hemen alır ve cihaz değişimi akışını internet varken başlatır. Böylece öğrenci bunu derste internetsizken öğrenmez. Eski anahtarla imzalanmış bekleyen kayıtlar yine gönderilir, yeni anahtarla verilenler değişim onaylanana kadar beklemede kalır. misses.finding: App Attest binds a key to the App ID, which is the App ID prefix (normally the 10-digit team ID) plus the bundle ID, and the server checks the RP ID hash against it. Apple DTS says keychain items in App-ID-prefix groups are lost when the prefix changes, and in June 2026 told a developer with device-bound keys to think seriously about not transferring the app at all. The plan leaves open whether an individual account can use unlisted App Store distribution (line 496). If the iPhone app later moves to another team, by transfer or as a new app, every iPhone binding has to be redone, which under line 84 means a face-to-face device change for every iPhone student.

Line 78 accepts such phones with instructor confirmation, but line 75 already asks every student for one bulk instructor confirmation, so the unverified phone faces no extra step; only the label differs, and the plan does not say what the label does. verdict_reason: No finding in this slice is high severity, and none is refuted or unverifiable: 7 CONFIRMED (S08-01, 02, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08) and 3 CORRECTED (S08-03 premise holds only on Android 13+ and its default choice clashes with the non-raisable 10,000 per day cap for a GitHub-only app; S08-09 other npm verifiers exist and node-app-attest carries three dependencies; S08-10 has no iPhone path without a successful attestKey). Recommendation issues on S08-02, 03, 04, 05, 09, 10 and the compactness note. Two checked_ok items disputed at low severity (Android 7.x attestation optional; asn1-android one KeyMint version behind). Five misses, none high: four medium (App Attest key loss without uninstall, Team ID change re-binds every iPhone, Play Integrity server decode missing from the plan, self-selected unverified path with an undefined label) and one low (UTF-8 string bytes).
